adjudication.rationale: The finding misunderstands how Rails migrations work. The `force: true` option in `create_table` only affects the migration when it runs - it will drop the table if it exists and recreate it. However, Rails migrations are designed to run only once per database. The migration system tracks which migrations have been applied in the schema_migrations table, so this migration will not be 'rerun' in normal operation. The `force: true` is commonly used to ensure clean table creation during initial migration runs or development resets. This is not a bug that would cause data loss in production - migrations don't get re-executed on deployed databases.
